messages:
Ashley: Heads-up — I noticed confusion in the console around saved queries: users expect per-route defaults but we also show per-model presets. Need to decide UX and API shape.
Maria: Agree, we've got two orthogonal concepts: route-scoped view vs model-scoped view. Users keep asking "why did my saved view disappear when I switched model?" :confused: 
Dan: Can we surface scope explicitly? e.g., a small badge 'route' or 'model' next to the saved view name and a tooltip that explains scope and quota attribution.
Kevin: On quota: if a saved view changes the sampling/aggregation and therefore telemetry volume, who owns the quota? Route owner? Model owner? Right now Console attributes to route.
Sophie: Proposal: default saved views created from Route UI are route-scoped; from Model picker are model-scoped. Allow cloning between scopes with a checkbox. Keep defaults consistent so behavior is predictable.
Ashley: UX sketch: show a pill with scope + an affordance to 'pin as default for this route'. If pinned and uses more telemetry, show an alert about quota impact before users confirm.
Maria: API thought — expose endpoints: 
```
GET /v1/routes/{route_id}/saved_views
GET /v1/models/{model_id}/saved_views
POST /v1/saved_views (body: {name, scope: "route" | "model", scope_id, filters, sample_rate})
```
We need clear contract for migrating a view from model -> route (and vice versa).
Dan: Also need console telemetry to record when a saved view is used for long-running compare jobs so Optimize and billing are accurate. Add an event: saved_view_applied with sample_rate and estimated_token_impact.
Kevin: Edge case: what happens on rollouts? If route is on canary with 10% traffic to new model, should route-scoped saved view reflect canary traffic split when computing cost? I think yes — the view applies to route traffic as routed. Need to show an estimated cost breakdown by variant in the UI.
Sophie: UX for that: small breakdown bar under the pinned view: 70% model-a, 30% model-b, est tokens/day: 1.2M. Clicking expands to per-variant cost.
Ashley: Implementation notes: backend needs to resolve scope at eval time. If scope == route, we expand to actual model variants via routing policy and attach telemetry tags: route_id, variant_id, saved_view_id.
Maria: We should also add an "ephemeral querybook" mode — quick ad-hoc queries that aren't persisted but show up in your session and don't affect saved_views quota. Users asked for one-off compare flows.
Dan: Ephemeral mode: client-side only, no server mutation. If user wants to persist, show "Save to route" or "Save to model" with a migration flow.
Sophie: For rollout UX, default to showing estimated costs for the last 7 days of similar traffic patterns. Add a tooltip: "Estimates use recent routing splits and sample rates — actual may vary."
Kevin: Security: only route admins can pin default saved views. Model-scoped views should be writable by model owners. Need RBAC checks in POST/PUT.
Ashley: Action items:
- Maria: draft API contract & migration endpoints (migration should create a new saved_view and mark old as migrated).
- Dan: add telemetry events + schema for saved_view_applied.
- Sophie: mockups for badge/pin UX + rollout breakdown.
- Kevin: spec RBAC rules for pin/save/migrate.
- Ashley: spike to show per-variant cost estimate in Console (2d).

Maria: I'll drop the API draft in this thread by EOD.
deploy-bot: New mock deployment available in staging: console/savedviews/ux-spike -> https://staging.redwood-inference.internal/console (expires in 48h) :rocket: 
Ashley: Nice, will review the staging flow and test ephemeral mode. Thanks everyone.
